messages:
cs-ops: Hi team — AcmeCorp reporting elevated latency and intermittent 429s hitting their Dedicated endpoint in prod-us-west during a short traffic spike (~14:22 UTC). They say their capacity didn't scale: observed QPS ~120, HPA desired ~6 but current stayed at 2. Ticket: https://support.redwood/acme/1234. Can someone triage?

devon: cc @maria @jake — any quick hypotheses? Customer says bursts last ~15s repeated over 2 minutes.

maria: pulling logs now. I already see autoscaler metric: "desired=6 current=2 pending=4" and several preflight probe timeouts on warmpool attach: "preflight probe failed: timeout 30s".

sre-bot: ALERT: autoscaler-scale-delay prod-us-west — desired_replicas > current_replicas for >120s (alert id: A-2149998895)

jake: quick thought — could be warmpool attach race combined with preflight probe window. Our warmpool attaches sometimes take ~45-60s when model CKPTs download; preflight/default timeout is 30s, so node doesn't reach Ready in time and isn't counted by the HPA.

alisa: commands to inspect:
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=dedicated-runtime -o wide
kubectl -n prod describe deployment dedicated-runtime
kubectl -n prod get events | grep -i attach

maria: logs snippet (trimmed):
[2026-03-15T14:22:45Z] attach: warmpool attach request for node-pool-3 start
[2026-03-15T14:23:15Z] kubelet: preflight probe timeout after 30s
[2026-03-15T14:23:50Z] attach: node registered but has taint: NoSchedule
[2026-03-15T14:24:05Z] autoscaler: scale_up skipped - insufficient ready nodes

devon: repro I ran locally (quick reproducer):
# burst 200 concurrent short generate requests
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' & done

sre-bot: NOTE: cluster config for this pool -> minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=10, warmPoolSize=1, preflight_timeout=30s

jake: hypothesis: model cache download (large ckpt blobs) + a noisy neighbor with high disk IO caused node init >30s. Node not Ready within preflight -> kube/controller didn't mark as usable -> autoscaler didn't reach desired ready count -> requests hit backpressure/429s. Also noticed one attach returned successful registration but kubelet kept the node tainted for ~35s.

alisa: immediate workaround: increase minReplicas for this customer to reduce chance of hitting cold attach on burst. Patch example:
kubectl patch hpa dedicated-runtime -n prod --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":4}]'

maria: metric stats for the pool: pod startup median ~58s, p90 ~120s. So current preflight_timeout=30s is too low for GPU-backed pods pulling models.
devon: customer-facing note draft:
"We're seeing delayed node readiness during short traffic spikes due to model cache download times. We're increasing min replicas and expanding the warm pool for your Dedicated capacity while we dig into root cause. This should significantly reduce the 429s during bursts."

cs-ops: action items: 1) temporary mitigation (increase minReplicas to 4 & warmPoolSize to 2), 2) infra follow-up to increase preflight_timeout for gpu-backed pools, 3) audit noisy-node disk IO and image/ckpt sizes, 4) evaluate async attach or progressive readiness signals. Who owns which?

jake: I'll own infra ticket INF-4321 to bump preflight_timeout to 90s for gpu-backed warmpool attaches and to run disk IO investigation on suspicious nodes (will attach timeline and affected node ids). Will also test increasing warmPoolSize to 2 in staging.

maria: runtime team will add more granular model-download progress logs and consider making readiness gates wait on model cache pull progress rather than a hard 30s probe. I'll open RT-214 for this.
devon: I'll apply the minReplicas change for AcmeCorp and monitor their ticket. Will post a follow-up here once we observe traffic for the next 30 minutes.

cs-ops: thanks all — please update the ticket and paste commands/output here when done.

alisa: quick note: also saw one kube event where image pull backoff + throttled registry pulls were present at 14:22:40 — may be contributing. I've copied registry team.

jake: adding a test plan: 1) simulate 200rps bursts in staging, 2) validate node readiness times under new preflight timeout, 3) verify HPA responds and that desired==ready within 90s, 4) if stable, roll change to prod with canary.

maria: I'll correlate model shard sizes to node init times and propose a caching optimization if needed.

devon: updated customer: "We've implemented a temporary capacity increase and are investigating root cause; we'll follow up within 2 hours."

cs-ops: :thumbsup: ping when INF-4321 is created and when minReplicas change is live.

sre-bot: TICKET_OPENED INF-4321 by jake at 2149999205

jake: INF-4321 created, assigned to infra. Will update.
